title: Subtype-resolved cardiac neighborhoods and asynchronous cardiomyocyte maturation after birth
central_message: A ventricular CM identity contains a range of maturation states within the same section. Resolving its fibroblast and endothelial neighbors at subtype level reveals component-specific developmental relationships that a broad CM–EC–fibroblast grouping cannot describe.
sections: CM identity and maturation are separate axes within P0 and P7 sections
Known fibroblast and endothelial subtypes define finer neighborhood profiles
Regional organization and local association answer different questions
Specific CM-state and maturation-component relationships emerge
Fibroblast program specialization provides temporal comparison sets
Transport is conditioned on CM identity and audited against held-out maturation
data_scope: Secondary analysis, one spatial section/age, no new biological replication
